description:
Metered: one Engine API call. Cut timber parts grouped by cross-section from matching stock lengths. Timber optimization (cross-section-aware 1D). Cut lengths from bars that have a CROSS-SECTION. Unlike `/v1/optimize/1d`, where every bar can serve every part, a 50×150 part can only come out of 50×150 stock — so the job is split by cross-section, each section is matched to its own stock and solved separately, and the response carries both per-section and job-wide totals.

Fanning the same job out into several `/v1/optimize/1d` calls is not equivalent: it costs one call per section against your quota, moves the stock matching to your code, and cannot distinguish "no material of this section" from "did not fit" — which this endpoint reports separately as `unmatched` and `unplaced`.

`sw` and `sh` may be given in either order: 50×100 and 100×50 are the same bar turned over and are matched as one section. The response reports the normalised short/long form.

engine.description: As in 1D, `max` is not offered here (a **400** before a call is charged). `balanced` resolves to the same packer as `heuristic`: within a section a timber job is a length problem, and free nesting has nothing to offer it. The value is accepted, echoed back, and a warning states which packer actually ran.

include.description: Three kinds of token. NARROWING (`cutPlan`, `offcuts`): omit the field entirely to get both; a present array keeps only the narrowing tokens it lists (an empty array drops both). ADDITIVE EXPORT (`svg`, `csv`, `dxf`): each adds an inline export STRING to the response (`svg` a standalone 2D layout — 2D only, a warning is returned for 1D/wood; `dxf` an R12/AC1009 drawing; `csv` a cut list, RFC 4180 quoted (a part name with a comma or a quote stays one field) and formula-injection-guarded (a name beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR is prefixed with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet reads it as text, not a formula — CWE-1236). 2D DATA (`labels`, `planHash`, `pdf`, `labelsPdf`): `labels` adds per-piece label data (`labels[]`, see `Label2D`), `planHash` a 64-hex fingerprint of the plan (the same plan always gives the same hash), `pdf` the cutting-plan PDF and `labelsPdf` the label PDF, both base64-encoded and drawn by the same code as the CutOptim app. These four are 2D only: a 1D or wood request returns a `warnings` entry instead. `pdf` renders at most 500 parts (total quantity); a larger 2D request with `pdf` is a 413 `too_large` with `details.path: "include"`. Export and data tokens do not affect narrowing, so `["svg"]` adds svg and — listing no narrowing token — drops cutPlan/offcuts; use `["cutPlan","offcuts","svg"]` to keep everything.

options.description: Identical to `Options1D` — a cross-section changes what fits, not how a bar is cut.

kerf.description: Blade width. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

minOffcut.description: Output filter: report a leftover only if it is at least this long.

mitrePairing.description: Pair parts of one section whose facing ends (`parts[].ends`) can share ONE saw cut. Off by default: a request without it is solved exactly as before. On, a plan with pairs is returned only when it ranks strictly better than the unpaired plan by the packer's own ranking (parts placed first, then material — or price with `minimizeCost`); otherwise the unpaired plan comes back. Pairs only, no chains of three or more.

respectStock.description: Treat `qty` as a hard cap. Applied PER CROSS-SECTION.

tolerance.description: Accept cuts overshooting by up to this much. Counted in `metrics.toleranceAcceptedCount` and noted in `warnings`.

trim.description: A bar has two ends, not four edges. `start` is the leading trim (it shifts the first part along the bar, so the first `pos` equals `start`); `end` is the trailing trim.

end.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

start.description: Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

items.description: A timber part. Same as a 1D part plus the CROSS-SECTION, which decides which stock it can come out of at all.

ends.description: Angled ends (mitre pairing). The `angle` is seen on `sh` AS ENTERED and the `bevel` on `sw`, so send the section the way the angles were measured.

end.description: One end cut of a part, in degrees from square (0 = a square end), signed. The part is measured long point to long point (`length` is its overall length). A part whose two end cuts would cross inside its section (shorter than its leads) cannot be made: a 400 `invalid_request` naming `parts[i].ends` says how long it must at least be.

angle.description: The face angle: the mitre or plumb cut as seen on the `depth` side (wood: on `sh` as entered).

bevel.description: The edge angle: the bevel as seen on the `thickness` side (wood: on `sw` as entered). A compound cut has both.

start.description: One end cut of a part, in degrees from square (0 = a square end), signed. The part is measured long point to long point (`length` is its overall length). A part whose two end cuts would cross inside its section (shorter than its leads) cannot be made: a 400 `invalid_request` naming `parts[i].ends` says how long it must at least be.

angle.description: The face angle: the mitre or plumb cut as seen on the `depth` side (wood: on `sh` as entered).

bevel.description: The edge angle: the bevel as seen on the `thickness` side (wood: on `sw` as entered). A compound cut has both.

flip.description: Mitre pairing only: which 180° turns of the part on the bar are allowed, so its angled end can meet a neighbour's. `none` (default — a profiled moulding or one-sided stock), `face` (end for end, the crown or top edge stays up — roof members), `edge` (end for end over the edge — flat stock, frames), `any`.

length.description: Cut length. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

material.description: Material identity — composes WITH the cross-section: two materials at the same 50×50 become two sections (a 50×50 Pine-Treated part cannot come from a 50×50 Pine-Untreated bar). Free string, library-independent. Absent = today's section-only grouping.

meta.description: Opaque JSON object (any keys) echoed back VERBATIM on the matching output (a part's meta on every placed piece of it; a stock row's meta on every sheet/rod cut from it). Attach ERP article numbers, order-line ids, customer refs to reconcile the cut plan with your system. Never parsed, never affects placement. Part meta follows its request row: the meta of each row lands on exactly its qty of placed pieces, even when rows share a name; stock meta by stock-row order.

name.description: Optional label. Defaults to `Part <1-based row index>`.

priority.description: Must-cut; wins stock when `options.respectStock` caps it. Applied WITHIN the part's own cross-section, since another section's bars could not have yielded it anyway.

qty.description: How many copies. The sum across all rows must not exceed 2000.

sh.description: The other side of the cross-section. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

sw.description: One side of the cross-section. ORDER DOES NOT MATTER — 50×100 and 100×50 are the same bar turned over and land in the same section. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

stock.description: At most 50 rows. Since every cross-section needs at least one stock row, this is also the practical ceiling on cross-sections in a single job; a wider catalogue should be split into several requests.

length.description: Bar length. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

material.description: A stock unit of material X serves only material-X parts. Free string; see the part `material`.

meta.description: Opaque JSON object (any keys) echoed back VERBATIM on the matching output (a part's meta on every placed piece of it; a stock row's meta on every sheet/rod cut from it). Attach ERP article numbers, order-line ids, customer refs to reconcile the cut plan with your system. Never parsed, never affects placement. Part meta follows its request row: the meta of each row lands on exactly its qty of placed pieces, even when rows share a name; stock meta by stock-row order.

name.description: Optional stock label, echoed back as `sections[].stockName` so a plan can name the material an operator has to fetch.

priority.description: "Use this stock up first" — a soft preference ranked BELOW sheet/rod count. Steers which format is spent first without spending more of it.

qty.description: Bars available. A hard cap only with `options.respectStock`.

sh.description: The other side of the cross-section. Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.

sw.description: One side of the cross-section (either order). Unit-agnostic: pick one unit (mm, inch, …) for every length in the request and every length in the response is in that same unit. Nothing is converted server-side.
